Funding & Sponsorship

Understanding Your Funding Options

Funding prosthetic or orthotic care can feel complicated. We're here to make it easier. Our team has decades of experience working with government funding programs, workplace benefits, private insurance and other funding organizations. We'll help you understand the coverage available to you, prepare the required documentation, and guide you through the approval process. You focus on your care — we'll help you navigate the funding.

Funding & Insurance FAQ

How Much Will I Have to Pay? +

There isn't one answer that applies to everyone. Your out-of-pocket cost will depend on the device recommended, your eligibility for government funding, and any private insurance or additional funding available to you. Before treatment proceeds, our team will review the expected cost with you and explain the funding and coverage that may apply. If you're unsure what coverage you have, don't worry — bring us whatever information you have and we'll help you determine the next steps.

How much does ADP cover? +

Ontario's Assistive Devices Program (ADP) provides funding toward eligible prosthetic and orthotic devices. For many eligible devices, ADP contributes up to 75% of the ADP approved price or maximum amount. This does not necessarily mean 75% of the total cost of every device. Our team will review the applicable ADP funding with you and explain any remaining costs before proceeding.

Does ADP cover all prosthetic components? +

No. ADP provides funding for many prosthetic devices and components, but not every component, feature or type of prosthesis is eligible for funding. Coverage also depends on your individual needs and the device prescribed. We will review the available ADP funding and discuss any additional costs or funding options with you.

Does ADP cover orthotic devices? +

ADP provides funding for certain eligible custom orthotic devices when program requirements are met. The amount and eligibility depend on the type of orthosis and your individual circumstances. Our team can help determine whether your prescribed device qualifies and guides you through the application process.

Can private insurance cover what ADP doesn't? +

Often, yes. Many extended health insurance plans provide coverage for prosthetic and orthotic devices and may help with costs not funded through ADP. Coverage varies considerably between plans. We can provide detailed estimates and supporting documentation to help you obtain preauthorization or submit your claim.

Do I need a prescription? +

Many funding programs and insurance providers require a prescription or other medical documentation before approving a prosthetic or orthotic device. Requirements vary depending on the device and funding source. If documentation is required, our team will explain what is needed and can work with your healthcare provider to help obtain it.

Do you submit the funding paperwork for me? +

In many cases, yes. Our team regularly prepares estimates, applications and supporting documentation for government funding programs, insurers and other funding organizations. Where direct submission is permitted, we can often coordinate the process on your behalf. If something needs to be completed or submitted by you or your healthcare provider, we'll let you know.

What if my injury happened at work? +

If your prosthetic or orthotic needs are related to an approved workplace injury or illness, funding may be available through the Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB). Hamilton Prosthetics & Orthotics is a preferred WSIB vendor with extensive experience supporting injured workers throughout the funding and treatment process. Our team can work directly with your WSIB case manager and healthcare team to coordinate treatment recommendations, estimates, and any supporting documentation required for approval — helping make the process as straightforward as possible.

Does ODSP or Ontario Works provide additional funding? +

Additional assistance may be available to eligible individuals receiving ODSP or Ontario Works, particularly for certain costs associated with ADP-funded devices and prosthetic supplies. Eligibility and coverage depend on the program and individual circumstances. Our team can help identify the funding that may apply to you.

Does The War Amps help with prosthetic costs? +

Yes, eligible amputees may receive financial assistance for prosthetic care through The War Amps, including its programs for children and adults. The amount and type of assistance depend on individual eligibility and the device being requested. We have experience working with The War Amps and can help prepare the estimates and documentation required for consideration.

How long does funding approval take? +

Approval times vary depending on the funding organization, the type of device being requested and whether additional medical or clinical information is required. Some approvals are relatively straightforward, while more complex requests can take longer. We will submit the required documentation as promptly as possible and keep you informed throughout the process.

What happens if my funding request is denied? +

A denial does not always mean there are no other options. We will review the reason for the decision and determine whether additional clinical information, clarification, reconsideration or another funding source may be appropriate. Where possible, we'll work with you and your healthcare team to explore the next steps.

Will I know how much I have to pay before you make my device? +

Yes. Before proceeding, we will review the estimated cost of your device, the funding or insurance coverage that has been confirmed, and any amount that will be your responsibility. Our goal is to make sure you understand the financial side of your care before treatment moves forward.

What if I don't know what funding or insurance I have? +

That's okay. You don't need to understand the funding system before contacting us. Bring us whatever information you have — such as your insurance details, WSIB claim information, or information about government benefits — and our team can help determine which funding options may apply.

Do I have to pay for my device upfront and get reimbursed? +

It depends on your funding source and insurance plan. In some situations, Hamilton Prosthetics & Orthotics can bill the funding organization or insurer directly. In others, you may be required to pay a portion and submit documentation for reimbursement. We will explain how billing will work in your particular situation before proceeding.

What if my insurance company asks for more information? +

This is common. Insurers may request prescriptions, clinical justification, treatment information, detailed estimates or additional documentation before approving a device. Our team regularly works with insurers and healthcare professionals to provide the clinical information required to support prosthetic and orthotic funding requests.
